newsitem.title: USA: Judge overturns Charles Keating III conviction.
newsitem.headline: Judge overturns Charles Keating III conviction.

text.p: A federal judge Tuesday ordered a new trial for Charles Keating III, the son of financier Charles Keating Jr., whose related conviction on fraud and racketeering charges was overturned Monday.

U.S. District Judge Mariana Pfaelzer ordered the new trial after lawyers argued that the jurors who convicted the Keatings for their role in the collapse of the Lincoln Savings and Loan had been tainted by their knowledge of a prior state court conviction on similar charges.

Charles Keating III had been found guilty on 64 counts of securities and wire fraud, conspiracy and racketeering in connection with 1989 the collapse of Lincoln, which cost taxpayers $2.6 billion and set off chain of savings and loan failures.
His father, owner of the now-defunct Lincoln, was accused of bilking thousands of elderly investors, and was later convicted on 73 federal counts of fraud and racketeering.
A status conference to set a new trial date for both Keatings was set for Jan. 16.
